note: Base cost recalibrated from 0.13 to 0.4 after a full calibration sweep (see paysim_cost_calibration.json) found the model's response to cost is bimodal on this 7-feature dataset: costs 0.13 and 0.2 collapse to ~99.6% deferral (defer everything), costs 0.3, 0.5, 0.65, 0.8 and 1.0 collapse to ~0% deferral (defer nothing) within 8 epochs. cost=0.4 was the only value found to settle into a stable, non-degenerate intermediate operating point, confirmed here over a full un-aborted 15-epoch run for both Model 2 and Model 3.
analysis: Standard L2D (Model 2) is nearly flat across High (0.69%) and Critical (0.68%) tiers -- it does not preferentially defer the highest-risk transactions, consistent with the pattern already found on ULB and IEEE-CIS. Risk-Sensitive L2D (Model 3) raises Critical-tier deferral to 3.84%, a 5.65x increase over Model 2's Critical-tier rate, while barely touching Low-tier deferral (0.02%). This is directionally consistent with both other datasets (ULB 4.6x-24.7x across 5 seeds; IEEE-CIS 3.8x Critical/Low ratio) despite PaySim's much narrower absolute deferral rates -- the effect holds even on this feature-poor (7-feature), highly imbalanced, difficult-to-calibrate dataset.
